newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs off sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs off sharply.

text.p: Selling prompted by an overbought condition pushed CME pork bellies down into sell stops and prices ended as much as limit down. Hog futures also hit sell stops on further general fund liquidation, traders said.

Pork bellies closed down the 3.000 cent limit in May through August with July ending at 89.025 cents. Other months were off 1.900 to 1.550. Hog futures ended 1.275 to 0.150 cent per lb lower with June off most at 81.050 cents.
Bellies appeared overbought as much of Thursday's run up for limit gains in July and August came on short-covering.

Early carryover fund demand and further unwinding of long hog/short pork belly spreads provided only temporary support and pork belly futures tumbled for limit losses. The large premium to cash and an overbought condition weighed heavily on the market and pushed prices down into sell stops which took 1997 contracts down the limit, traders said.
"We had just too much of a historical premium to cash bellies," said Jason Roose from U.S. Commodities Inc.
Spillover weakness from hog futuers was also cited after the second day of sharp losses there, traders said.
"Bellies tried to rally without hogs and they just couldn't handle it them by themselves," one trader said.
Refco, LFG and R.J. O'Brien sold after Rosenthal Collins, Fimat Futures USA and RBH bought, pit sources said.
Early indications on next week's monthly Cold Storage report ranged from 52.2 to 59 million lbs on hand May 1 compared with 54.8 million on hand April 1 and 57.2 million a year earlier.
Carryover fund liquidation and technical selling pushed hog futures down. The market turned technically weak when the packers announced they would be cutting kills, traders said.
Expectations are for cash hogs to trade another $1 per cwt Monday after declining $1 to $2 Thursday, traders said.

Hogs turned technically weak after falling to one-month lows and pushing through chart support Thursday. Added technical pressure early hit sell stops to send June down to its lowest level since April 9. Although futures were at a discount to the lean index, the index is expected to move lower, they said.

R.J. O'Brien, Cargill Investor Services and locals notably sold. In hog options, First Chicago actively sold June 78 puts and also sold August 86 calls. ADM Investor Services bought July 90 calls, pit sources said.
